They say nothing about how PonsV2BondingCurve actually prices a buy or a sell, because the production contract does not use this library the way these tests do:   buy   fee and creator tax are computed on the quote INPUT and subtracted         before the curve is called, and the curve is called with feeBps = 0   sell  the curve is called with feeBps = 0 to get grossQuoteOut, then fee         and tax are taken OUT OF THE OUTPUT   both  the tradeable reserve excludes accrued fees:         phantomQuote + trackedQuote - quoteFeeBalance - creatorTaxBalance So on the trade paths the library is always called with feeBps = 0. Fee and reserve accounting has to be proven against the real contract, and is not proven here. The parameter is NOT dead, though: PonsV2LaunchFactory._requireQuotable passes the real curveFeeBps into quoteAmountOut as a launch-time sanity check that the configured curve can price a reference buy at all. So test_lib_fee* below does describe a path that runs in production - just that guard, not a trade. The decimal-invariance tests below are likewise about the pure formula with exactly scalable inputs. The real contract floors fee and tax to integers, so small amounts can diverge between an 8- and an 18-decimal quote. That tolerance belongs in the contract-level tests, not IS_TEST().notice: Marker used by Forge to identify test contracts.

testFuzz_lib_quoteDecimalsInvariant(uint.notice: Fuzzed, so the claim is not resting on chosen numbers.

test_lib_curveShapeDependsOnRatioNotScal.notice: The economics doc claims the SHAPE depends only on threshold / (threshold + phantomQuote). Same ratio, different absolute scale, must reach the same fraction of supply.

test_lib_feeIsEquivalentToShrinkingTheIn.notice: LIBRARY BEHAVIOUR ONLY - see the scope note. Not the product's fee model: the real buy subtracts fee and tax from the input itself and then calls the curve with feeBps = 0.

test_lib_feeReducesOutputMonotonically().notice: LIBRARY BEHAVIOUR ONLY. The production buy and sell paths pass feeBps = 0 and handle the fee outside the curve, so this proves a property of the library, not of a trade. See the scope note above.

test_lib_getAmountIn_revertsAtFullFee().notice: A 100% fee has no input that produces output.

test_lib_getAmountIn_revertsBeyondReserv.notice: getAmountIn cannot promise more output than the reserve holds.

test_lib_getAmountIn_roundTripsWithoutLo.notice: getAmountIn must ask for at least what getAmountOut would consume.

test_lib_quoteAmountOut_returnsZeroInste.notice: quoteAmountOut is the non-reverting variant: same answer, or zero.

test_lib_quoteDecimalsDoNotChangeTokensO.notice: Scaling the quote side down by 1e10 must not change how many tokens a proportionally scaled buy returns.

test_lib_quoteDecimalsInvariant_acrossSi.notice: The same invariance across a spread of trade sizes, including one large enough to move the curve hard.

test_lib_revertsWhenOutputRoundsToZero().notice: A dust trade against a huge reserve rounds to zero out, and that must revert rather than silently take the input.

test_lib_roundTripCannotProfit().notice: Buying then selling back must never return more quote than was spent.
